Subject: XFN weekly sync: action audit + exec asks for QBR prep

Hi all —

Quick follow-up from this morning's weekly sync. I pulled together an action audit focused on the QBR asks that execs flagged last week and the cross-functional exceptions we still have open. Two explicit requests from the execs that need prioritized:

1) Canary rollouts: confirmation of owners and gating criteria (latency SLO, rollback windows, observability runbooks).
2) Procurement + SOC2 evidence: Nimbus needs an ETA for SOC2 artifacts and a procurement contact for contract redlines.

Please see the short asks below and update by EOD tomorrow where you own an item. I'll consolidate into the QBR document on Thursday morning.

OPEN ACTIONS (initial):
- Owner: karthik_iyer — Define canary gating matrix (latency thresholds, sample sizes) and provide expected completion date.
- Owner: marissa_cole — Add canary matrix to QBR doc + attach any verification test plans.
- Owner: vivek_kulkarni — Confirm infra capacity for dedicated canary pools and any reservation needs.
- Owner: procurement@nimbushealth.com / Oliver — Confirm procurement timeline and required evidence bundle (SOC2, data retention policy).

Attachments: reference doc placeholder (I'll add the working QBR matrix link after I hear back).

Thanks — short updates are fine (1-2 lines).

— Soojin
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from our side:

- Procurement is aiming to finish redline review the week of Dec 20. We need a formal evidence bundle for SOC2 and a contact for any follow-up questions.
- For SOC2 we typically need: attestation PDF, SC and SA descriptions, data retention policy, and a point of contact who can respond within 48 hours during our review.

I'll coordinate with procurement (cc'd) and share a simple checklist by EOD tomorrow. If Redwood can provide the SOC2 attestation and a short summary of your logging/audit retention practices, that will speed things up.

— Oliver

Nimbus Health

On Tue, Dec 14, 2026 at 09:00, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick follow-up from this morning's weekly sync.

Thanks — tagging in details from the runtime team. A few clarifications:

- Canary gating: I'll own the gating matrix. Planned deliverable: a short spreadsheet with the following columns: metric, target, sample size, rollback trigger, owner. ETA: 2026-12-17 COB.
- Latency SLO: for the initial canary we recommend a 1.5x of production baseline for 95th p99 spikes; we will call out strict rollback at >2x and sustained for >3 minutes.
- Observability: Vivek, can you confirm whether the canary pools will have trace-level retention for 7 days or if we should extend? The execs want the ability to replay traces during the QBR window.

I'll add a small test harness to the matrix for A/B traffic split tests (10/90 then 25/75) and mark the rollback gates.

— Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
